A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on cross-entropy loss, training efficiency, multiple-SAE adaptation, SAEBench, feature steering, and general language capabilities, with additional results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds capability results for an adapted model without an SAE and for Gemma-2-27B in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 retains the frozen SAE and base-model weights, trainable LoRA adapters, KL-divergence objective, and TopK/JumpReLU layer restrictions. The additional LoRA-only evaluation does not revise the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets, SAEBench tasks, steering domains, and MMLU, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA coverage remain unchanged. Table 5 expands model configurations within existing tasks, without introducing different data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds the adapted model without an SAE, labeled LoRA, as an evaluated comparison condition alongside Original, SAE, and SAE + LoRA. The TopK/e2e and SAEBench comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 expands from three to four conditions by evaluating LoRA with the SAE removed, and Table 5 extends capability testing to Gemma-2-27B. Figure 1 also corrects its training-budget caption from 4B to 2B tokens, matching the existing descriptions in both versions; this does not establish changed training or reruns.

E4.justification: The new LoRA-without-SAE control tests whether adaptation preserves general capabilities when the SAE is removed. Existing single-layer ablations, token-loss analysis, activation-distance analysis, and steering analyses, including their appendix results, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report one standard error in Table 5 and 90% confidence intervals over 500 examples for steering in Table 4. Added results retain the existing reporting convention; no new run counts, seed information, or statistical procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: Previously reported results are retained. Table 5 adds LoRA-only scores for 2B/9B and four-condition results for 27B, extending one existing capability study. Outcomes are mixed: new 9B LoRA MMLU is 68.8 versus 70.0 for Original, while new 27B SAE + LoRA BLEU is 38.9 versus 40.9 for SAE.

T1.justification: The method equations, steering formulation, and Appendix A.2 metric definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit claim that adaptation does not harm general language-model capabilities. The central proposal, novelty claim, cross-entropy improvements, efficiency claims, and listed contributions otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 newly acknowledges that improved discovery of faithful circuits has not been demonstrated. Section 5.3 interprets the expanded capability results as showing no harm, although some reported scores decrease. Section 6.2 mainly restates the existing activation-distance interpretation.

D1.justification: Removing the acknowledgments also removes v1's disclosure that SAE training used EleutherAI/sae infrastructure. The authors' own code link, existing experimental details, and appendix data-generation prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The new Impact Statement adds Sharkey et al. (2025) on mechanistic-interpretability open problems and Slattery et al. (2024) on AI risks. This modestly expands safety-oriented positioning; the methodological related-work discussion and novelty comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the abstract and Sections 5.3, 6.2, and 7.1, a new Impact Statement, removal of acknowledgments, and an added conference-publication notice. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 becomes a wider display with an additional condition and model block, shifting later material. Existing plots are retained. Figure 11 corrects its panel references from Top/Bottom to Left/Right, although its added closing sentence is unfinished.

improvement.justification: The added LoRA-without-SAE control and 27B results in Table 5 modestly strengthen empirical validation, while the new circuit-faithfulness limitation improves qualification. These benefits outweigh limited disclosure and editing regressions. However, the broader no-harm claim needs qualification: new results include lower scores, notably 9B LoRA MMLU at 68.8 versus 70.0 for Original. The core method and most supporting evidence remain unchanged.
